title: Skin without Underwear
content:
I want to create underwear and need to use an avatar without underwear texture to use it for my presentation. I'm not able to change the skin in the newest CLO version. How can I solve this problem? In addition the question: is it possible that the avatars like Feifei can be added back to the default garment avatars? I was always using FeiFei and like to continue using her.

Hope we can find a solution.

Sophie

PS.: In my opinion the new way of reaching the library is not an improvement.


### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi There. For the newer Avatars the undergarments can be set to nude, this has been a feature in CLO for several versions now. You can click on the avatar and the go to the Property Editor > Body Styling > Click on the blue head icon to the right on Skin Style > a pop up will open > Change underwear from Covered to NudeAs for older Avatars these will not be added back to to CLO library. But if you wish to continue using FeiFei you can open an old CLO project where you used FeiFei and then go to File > Save As Avatar. You can save FeiFei, just make sure to save to your local computer/sharedirve and not to the CLO program folders as those can be replaced when CLO is updated in the future.Also, keep in mind that FeiFei and older avatars will not have some of the newer features like bust adjustment, soft body, or the above mentioned Skin Style options
content_description: This web page aims to provide solutions for creating a custom avatar without underwear texture in CLO software and to discuss the possibility of restoring the Feifei avatar to the default garment options.

title: Unlocking VMOD Magic Outside CLO: Fur Strand Breakthrough!
content:
* * *

Hi everyone!  
I’m **beyond excited** to share something I just discovered that completely **changed my workflow** – and I _had_ to post it here because I know I can’t be the only one who needed this!

🔍 I’ve always loved working with **VMODs** for fabrics in CLO, but as someone who renders mainly in external software (Unreal, Blender, etc.), I always felt limited – like I was missing the full power of those textures outside of CLO. Until now.

✨ I started experimenting with **Fur Strands inside VMODs** , and the results blew my mind. Turns out, you can totally **bake strand-based effects directly into the 3D model** , and then render them outside of CLO – without rebuilding the entire shader from scratch. No more starting from zero to simulate that delicate fiber look!

* * *

🔄 Before & After – Render Comparison

![1909bd239af846589b549ce418e393bd](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202505/2014fe3da04741ff949f9c1465d403b7/images/1909bd239af846589b549ce418e393bd1.png)**Left:** VMOD 3D with Fur Strand  
**Right:** Original VMOD 3D  
What’s crazy is this used to be **just a render-time effect**. But now… it’s **actual geometry inside the 3D view**! No tricks, no illusions – those fibers are **real mesh strands** you can see and work with before even hitting render.

* * *

### 🧵 True 3D Vision – No More “Render-Only” Magic

![41a5e9f5e5e7453185cdf320e069adf4](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202505/2014fe3da04741ff949f9c1465d403b7/images/41a5e9f5e5e7453185cdf320e069adf42.png)

On the left: **VMOD with Fur Strand** – you can clearly see the strand geometry right inside the 3D viewport.  
On the right: Original VMOD – the texture is there, but it’s just a visual placeholder until render.  
  
And here’s the amazing part:

🔁 **Once you copy over the fur settings** (shape, density, roughness map, etc.),  
🎯 The **final render looks almost identical** to the original!  
But now you’re working with actual geometry — not a preset shader effect that only comes alive at render time.

This opens up a whole new world of flexibility:  
✅ You can preview and tweak fur in real time.  
✅ Export it to external engines like Unreal or Blender.  
✅ And finally bridge the gap between **hyperrealism and workflow control**.  


* * *

### 💡 Why This Matters (at least to me!)

This discovery means:

  * I can **re-use** my entire library of custom VMODs outside CLO.

  * No need to rebuild complex shaders in other tools.

  * Textures look **richer, fuzzier, and closer to real fabric** , especially for knits, fleece, and delicate materials.




Honestly, it felt like unlocking a **secret power-up**. If you’ve ever wanted to push the realism of your renders while keeping a smooth pipeline, **this is for you**.

* * *

### 🔧 Super Tip!

When transitioning from _Fur Render_ (render-only) to _Fur Strand_ (real-time), some settings reset or behave differently — but with a few adjustments, you can recreate the original look or even enhance it.

Here’s my personal checklist and advanced tips after testing:

✅ **Base, Normal, Metallic, Displacement texture**  
→ This is preserved. No changes needed.

⚠️ **Fur parameters**  
→ These reset, so you’ll need to reapply:

  * Hair shape

  * Shine

  * Gravity

  * Curl

  * Variation

  * **Roughness** → Switch from value to **map** input for more accurate surface behavior.

  * **Density & Seed** → Play with different seed settings to discover subtle or dramatic variations. A single seed change can alter the entire flow without touching the base design.




🌓 **Opacity Map**  
→ I recommend **increasing contrast** , especially in darker areas, to restore the sense of translucency and depth seen in the original render. Without this, the material can look flat or less realistic.

🧩 **Custom Density Mapping (Advanced)**  
→ If your fabric has different fur behavior in specific areas (e.g. front vs. sides), unlink them:

  * Separate the textile into **front and side sections** using the properties editor

  * This lets you control **density, length, and hair direction** by faces.




* * *

### 🗣️ I’d love to hear from others:

Have you tried integrating strand-based textures into your external workflow?  
Any tips, feedback, or renders you want to share?

  
👀 Can you tell which one this is?  
  
![fbd6d41e40ae4f5c973bdb717e841ef8](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202505/2014fe3da04741ff949f9c1465d403b7/images/fbd6d41e40ae4f5c973bdb717e841ef8VMOD%203D%20ORIGINAL.png)

Thanks for reading!  
— Seer  
![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202505/2014fe3da04741ff949f9c1465d403b7/images/a356275c837f4137ac1e77ca099f22c63.png)
